props.title: Sodoma's Ghost

sections.content: **Sodoma's Ghost** (1988) represents a fascinating entry in Italian horror maestro Lucio Fulci's later filmography, coming during a period when Italian genre cinema was struggling to maintain its identity. Unlike his earlier gore-heavy classics like **The Beyond** (1981) and **City of the Living Dead** (1980), this supernatural thriller takes a more atmospheric approach, blending Nazi occultism with ghost story elements. The film's setup - involving a group of young people encountering supernatural forces in an abandoned hotel with a dark WWII history - echoes earlier European horror films like **Hotel of the Damned** (1977).

sections.content: The late 1980s marked a transitional period for Italian horror, with directors like Fulci struggling to adapt to changing audience tastes. **Demons** (1985) and **Demons 2** (1986) from Lamberto Bava represented more commercially-oriented approaches, while films like **Sodoma's Ghost** attempted to maintain connections to the more artistically ambitious Italian horror tradition of the 1970s, albeit with limited budgets and resources. SUBHEAD: Nazi Occultism in Horror Cinema

The film's use of Nazi occultism connects it to a broader tradition including **The Keep** (1983) and **Shock Waves** (1977). While lacking the production values of later entries like **Hellboy** (2004), **Sodoma's Ghost** maintains an effective creepy atmosphere through its isolated hotel setting and supernatural elements, even as it struggles with some dated effects and pacing issues typical of late 80s Italian horror.
